title: test(client): the auth envelope suite reads one registration and one sign-in instead of building one per case
body:
Part of #23181
Clause-②: no

Slice 2 of the test-budget card: the `@objectstack/client` row, which has two files. This PR takes one of them, `packages/client/src/auth-login-register-envelope.test.ts`. It does not claim `packages/client/src/auth-rotated-session-token.test.ts`; see "The rotated-token file" below. Test files only: one file changed, and `skip-changeset` applies by its criterion, because nothing in the package's `files[]` moves.

## What changed

`auth-login-register-envelope.test.ts` judges the result of a `register()`, a `login()` or both in 16 cases. None of them writes: no case changes the server's state or the returned values. Yet 13 of them built their own fresh engine, `AuthManager` and real scrypt sign-up (and a sign-in on top for most) only to read that value. They now read ONE registration and ONE sign-in of that user (`theRegistration()`, `theSignIn()`). It is built lazily, inside the first case that asks for it, so the work stays inside a clock. The shared engine is shut down once, in `afterAll`.

Unchanged: the module-scope warm-up and its pin ⑦, every `expect(` (47 = 47), and every it/describe title (the sha256 of the title lines is identical at `252775d1d` and `9a7f5bd95`). The header gains a section that says why, and that a case that writes builds its own `scenario()`.

## Where the wall went (measured before changing anything)

Box: 4 vCPU, shared with sibling agents; every run went through `os-verify-lock`. "Clocked" is the file line's duration in vitest's default reporter, the one CI's `report-test-timings.mjs` reads: hooks plus tests, collection excluded. Runs had `AI_AGENT` and `CLAUDECODE` unset, so vitest picks that reporter.

| file | card (CI, run `38319885190`) | isolated here, before (5 runs, `252775d1d`) | whole package here, before |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| envelope | 21.0 s | 4445 / 4789 / 4520 / 4706 / 4886 ms (median 4706) | 5716 ms |
| rotated-token | 14.6 s | 3108 / 3072 / 3234 / 3280 / 3517 ms (median 3234) | 4114 ms |

Both files run under 10 s on this box. The card's readings are about 4.5x the isolated median for both files, and 3.5 to 3.7x the whole-package reading. Neither file, nor anything it waits on, has a sleep, timer, retry or network hop. Per test:

- **envelope:** 13 cases took 188 to 556 ms each. Each was a fresh engine sync plus one or two real sign-ups and a sign-in. The other 3 cases ran in 0 to 2 ms. A scrypt probe (an untracked copy that wraps `node:crypto.scrypt`, not committed) counted **27 production-parameter derivations, 2737 ms of the 4819 ms** clocked in that run.
- **rotated-token:** 7 cases took 227 to 762 ms each. Every one uses a fresh user whose credentials that case changes (password, TOTP enrolment, rotation). The probe counted **18 derivations, 1752 ms of 3310 ms**. 9 of the 18 re-derive an input already derived (same password, same salt).

## After

| file | isolated here, after (3 runs, `9a7f5bd95`) | whole package here, after |
|:--|--:|--:|
| envelope | 406 / 510 / 512 ms (median 510) | 969 ms (`9a7f5bd95`); 1027 ms (`072fd4241`, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/client test`) |

The first case now pays the one arrangement (347 to 440 ms). ④'s login case takes 29 to 39 ms, ⑤'s `/get-session` case 14 to 18 ms, and the rest 0 to 7 ms. At the card's ratio (about 4.5x isolated), 510 ms projects to about 2.3 s in the hourly battery. That projection is an estimate; the card's own pin, the next refresh list, decides.

The after-change whole-package runs were on a busier box: the whole suite took 97.6 to 100.2 s against 61.9 s before. In those runs the unchanged rotated-token file read 7129 to 7276 ms, against 4114 ms before. That 1.7x swing on an untouched file is the same contention the card's seconds carry.

## The rotated-token file (row not claimed)

Its cases cannot share an arrangement. Each case changes its own user's credential state, and the first sign-up on an environment shuts self-registration, so each case needs a fresh engine and manager. What remains is the file's own behaviour.

One measured lever exists and is not taken here: plugin-auth's test-only scrypt memo (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/__tests__/scrypt-memo.testkit.ts`, from #23184). It answers a repeated derivation with the bytes the real call produced. In a probe it took this file from 3310 ms to 2433 to 2610 ms (9 of 18 derivations answered from the memo), about 24% less. At the card's ratio that still projects to about 11 s. Adopting it needs either a second copy of that testkit in `packages/client` or one shared home for it. That choice belongs to the seat, not to this slice, and the report carries the options.

## Proof the shared arrangement still fails when its subject breaks

Three ablations at the committed `9a7f5bd95`, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. Both subjects load from source: the test imports `./index`, and `vitest.config.ts` aliases `@objectstack/plugin-auth` to `src/`. So there is no dist leg. The predicted direction before each run was red.

- **[A]** The client's session lift stops writing `success` (`packages/client/src/index.ts`). Result: 5 red, 11 green (① ×2, ② ×2, and ③'s `data.session` case). Predicted 5, observed 5.
- **[B]** `auth.login` stops arming `client.token`. Result: 2 red (④'s login case and ⑤'s same-row case). Predicted 2, observed 2.
- **[C]** plugin-auth stops attaching the session to the credential response (`session-envelope-completion.ts`). Result: 7 red (② ×2, ③'s `success` case, ⑤ ×4). Predicted 6. The extra one is ③'s `success` case: its exhaustive issue list also gains `data.session`, so the red is correct.

Each restore was proven: the blob equals HEAD (`29bd23c088af`, `e701c4763eef`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Tests and gates

Every reading below is at `072fd4241` (a merge of `origin/main` `fa6a6085c`), taken after the last commit.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/client test`: 51 files and 663 tests passed, exit 0. In that run the envelope file read 1027 ms and the rotated-token file 7129 ms.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/client typecheck`: exit 0. `check:test-typecheck` is OK, with 0 entries in the debt ledger. The changed file is in the `tsconfig.test.json` program (`tsc --listFilesOnly`: 1 hit).
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 51 commands for the one changed path. 49 exited 0 on the first pass. Two answered exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET, because they read built output (`check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`). After a full `turbo run build` (76/76 tasks), the same two commands exited 0: 263 prose examples type-check, and 110 require entry points across 68 packages load. `--ran`: "51 derived, 51 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN."
- Lint, which `dispatch-gates` does not name: `eslint packages/client --no-inline-config` linted 57 files, the changed file among them, with 0 errors, 0 warnings and 0 fatal, exit 0. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.
- Every family CI runs is read from this PR's own check runs.

## Acceptance notes

- The `auth-rotated-session-token.test.ts` row stays open, as described above. The measured lever is plugin-auth's scrypt memo testkit, which currently lives only in that package; the report's open question carries the choice. Not filed.
- The card's per-file seconds are the slowest of 20 contended hourly runs. On this box both files read about 4.5x lower isolated, and an untouched file swung 1.7x between two whole-package runs here. A file's own clocked work is what a test-side change can move.
